comparison: Perfect agreement on structural quality claims (C1-C5). Both evaluations confirm high-resolution structures with appropriate experimental conditions. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the quality and unambiguous assignment of side chains.

Agreement on structural similarity claims (C13-C17). Both accept the quantitative measurements and structural comparisons. Peer review notes findings are 'mostly confirmatory' which aligns with OpenEval's assessment of well-supported structural similarity.

Partial overlap on W366F mutant characterization. OpenEval focuses on C20-C24 (functional and structural properties), while peer review encompasses broader claims including inactivated state details (C30-C36) and symmetry analysis (C37-C39). Both support the findings as confirmatory of enlarged selectivity filter in inactivation.

OpenEval evaluates detailed inactivated state structural measurements (C25-C36), which peer review groups with W366F characterization claims. Both find the structural details of the inactivated state well-supported and confirmatory.

OpenEval addresses symmetry analysis (C37-C39) separately, while peer review includes these with broader W366F findings. Both accept the negative result that no asymmetry was detected at 2.5 Å resolution.

Perfect agreement on VSD conformational changes (C40-C46). Both accept the quantitative measurements without challenge. Peer review's general praise of structural quality supports these detailed observations.

Partial overlap on DTx background. OpenEval evaluates toxin structure and Lys5 importance (C47-C51) as appropriately cited background, while peer review encompasses broader DTx findings including structural details (C52-C57, C94). Both support the toxin-related claims.

OpenEval focuses on DTx-bound state structural details (C52-C58), while peer review groups these with broader toxin findings. Both note the improved DTx structure and well-founded conclusions. Peer reviewers specifically highlight the surprising empty external K+ binding sites.
Strong agreement on background literature (C59-C62). OpenEval evaluates these as appropriate citations for varied K+ channel responses, peer review accepts them as valid context without challenge.

Agreement on Na+ structure findings (C63-C64) despite acknowledged limitations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to inability to distinguish Na+ from K+, while peer review rates as SUPPORTED, noting these are 'new findings of interest.' Both acknowledge the ion discrimination limitation.

Agreement on NaK2K model citations (C72-C75). Both accept these as appropriate mechanistic context for understanding C-type inactivation as filter destabilization.
Agreement on selectivity filter expansion measurements (C76-C78). OpenEval evaluates explicit quantitative measurements, peer review accepts these as part of confirmatory comparative analyses.
Agreement on MD simulation and functional measurement citations (C79-C83). Both accept the integration of computational and experimental data from cited sources as valid context.
Agreement on gating charge and inactivation mechanism citations (C84-C85). Both accept these as appropriate references for mechanistic interpretation.
Agreement on Kv1.3 comparisons and functional results (C86-C89). Both accept these as valid context and supporting evidence for physiologically relevant inactivated states.
